concepts.def: The first stage of converting a raw food into a usable form, such as milling wheat into flour or pasteurising milk.
Turning processed ingredients into food products, such as baking flour into bread or making milk into cheese and yoghurt.
Methods such as freezing, canning, drying and pickling that extend shelf life by slowing or preventing microbial growth and spoilage.
Substances added to food to preserve it or improve its colour, flavour or texture, such as preservatives, emulsifiers and antioxidants.
A heat treatment that destroys harmful bacteria in liquids such as milk by heating briefly to a set temperature then rapidly cooling.
Making large quantities of a standardised food product on a production line to a consistent specification at a lower cost per item.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Food Processing and Production — a core area of GCSE Home Economics: Food and Nutrition.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Food Processing and Production brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Food Processing and Production.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Milling wheat grains into flour is an example of:
options: Primary processing
Secondary processing
Preservation
Pasteurisation

mcqs.q: Heating milk briefly to destroy harmful bacteria then cooling it is called:
options: Pasteurisation
Fermentation
Dehydration
Homogenisation

mcqs.q: Freezing, canning and drying are all methods of food:
options: Preservation
Seasoning
Labelling
Branding

mcqs.q: An emulsifier added to mayonnaise is an example of a food:
options: Additive
Nutrient
Allergen
Contaminant

mcqs.q: What is the difference between primary and secondary processing?
options: Adds extra vitamins to the milk.
Primary processing only happens to meat.
Primary turns a raw food into a usable ingredient; secondary turns ingredients into food products.
They are the same stage with different names.

mcqs.q: What does pasteurisation do to milk?
options: Adds extra vitamins to the milk.
Heats it briefly to destroy harmful bacteria, then cools it, making it safer.
Additives are added only to increase the price.
Removes all bacteria so the milk lasts forever.

mcqs.q: Why are additives used in food?
options: Additives are always harmful chemicals with no purpose.
Adds extra vitamins to the milk.
Additives are added only to increase the price.
To preserve food or improve its colour, flavour or texture.
